I found no problems in PR #12, so it's fine to merge. There is one thing to check in the `superagent` profile first: its default model is no longer Gemini, which goes against your earlier "leave Gemini as default".

**The PR diff** (at commit `4bba9e7`; open, no conflicts):
- It adds one new file, `MULTI_MODEL_INTEGRATION.md`, and changes nothing else in the repo.
- It contains no secrets or profile files.

**The terms-of-use caveat is accurate.** I reloaded [Anthropic's legal and compliance page](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance) and both quoted phrases appear on it word for word:
- "is designed to support ordinary use of Claude Code and other native Anthropic applications"
- "should use API key authentication"

Its references to section 5 (operational notes) and section 6 (adding API keys) point to the right sections.

**The `superagent` default model changes are set up correctly.** These live only on your machine and aren't part of the PR.
- The main default is `openai-codex` / `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- "Next steps" uses `anthropic` / `claude-haiku-5-5`.
- Both are models the profile has set up, and the profile config check (`dsh --profile superagent --dump-config`) passes and shows exactly these values.

**Things to look at before or after merging:**
1. **Default model:** last time I looked, `web` still defaulted to Gemini. Someone changed `superagent` to `gpt-6.1-sol` at 15:12, and Gemini's `reasoningEffort: high` setting went with it. Revert it if that wasn't intended.
2. **"Next steps" on the Claude subscription:** it runs on the subscription login, so the terms caveat applies to it. It also shares that subscription's rate limit, which caused the earlier 429 failure on this ticket.
3. **Composio key:** the `superagent` profile file still has the Composio key written out in plain text as a fallback value.

None of these is in the PR. If the default model change is fine with you, merge with:

```
gh pr merge 12 --merge --repo gera3d/superagent-sandbox
```

report.summary:
Out of scope for this ticket's inferred (proactive) mandate, so I stopped without changing anything.

What issue #14 asks for: (1) trim `dsh-superagent/prompts/*.md` to a <4,500-token baseline; (2) enforce bash stdout truncation at 100 lines / 4 KB with full logs persisted to disk; (3) a new progress-heartbeat protocol every 2–3 actions; (4) add `TOKEN_OPTIMIZATION_GUIDE.md` to gera3d/superagent-sandbox.

Why dropped: this ticket was auto-accepted under matched rules, so `mandateInstructions` marked it inferred. That injects the restriction "limited to a small change internal to one module; no behavior changes ... report dropped" (`src/executor/dsh.ts:92`), and `prompts/admission.md:55` states the same scope for inferred tickets: "Ticket scope is limited to a small internal change in the deployment's repository; no public interface, product promise, behavior, new interaction or cross-module redesign." The request fails all three bounds: it changes runtime behavior (stdout truncation, heartbeat), spans modules (prompt text + executor/tool output handling + docs), and its prompt-edit target is not in the deployment repository gera3d/superagent-sandbox at all — the live prompts live in the separately checked-out `dsh-superagent` plugin package (`/Users/gerayeremin/Documents/deepseek-harness/default-workspace/dsh-superagent`, remotes gera3d/dsh-superagent-prototype + upstream), while the sandbox repo currently holds only three docs.

Also unresolved without a person: which prompt clauses to cut under the 4,500-token target (the 50 KB of prompts encode merge, review-round, trailer-credit, delivery-evidence and subscription rules that cannot be dropped safely on an autonomous guess), and the heartbeat's transport/state semantics. These are exactly the "product decisions / behavior change" stop conditions.

No files were modified, no branch or PR created. The human can authorize this by explicitly addressing the agent on issue #14 (mention), which routes it as an explicit request instead of an inferred proactive ticket; the work then needs a reviewable delivery for the prompt files, not only the sandbox doc.

Delivered the backlog autopilot in [PR #59](https://github.com/gera3d/superagent-sandbox/pull/59): `skills/autopilot/SKILL.md` (composes the existing pr-reviewer skill; adds the backlog loop, documented-answer rule, same-account comment path, serialized creative-mode apply handoff, and the six true-decision classes) and `reports/AUTOPILOT_BACKLOG.md` (every open PR with verdict/head/next step, apply issues, answered questions, decisions, checks, limitations). PR is MERGEABLE/CLEAN with no checks configured; no merge CLI is configured, so a person merges it.

Backlog run: all 19 open PRs reviewed once at their current head — 18 PASS (15 docs/report merge proposals, 3 plugin-code) and 1 FAIL (#46 model hierarchy: fresh worktree `c939e07` fails `tests/styles.spec.ts` because `src/client/client.css:108` splits `.dt-star` across lines; base `f3f6106` passes; 1 failed / 1386 passed). Code checks: #40 1434 tests pass; #39 3 pass and tree identical to `25d1781`; #44 1438 pass; #52 reproduced exactly (1556 passed / 2 skipped; 18 + 20 client); #46 fail. Secret scans of diffs, added files and PR bodies: 0 matches, values never printed. Patch checks: #39 applies to `b807422`, #46 to `f3f6106`, #49 reverse-applies to the live profile. Report claims spot-checked read-only.

Apply issues created in the required order: #55 Phase 0 → #56 slim panel → #57 OpenAI ranker → #58 model hierarchy. All are NEEDS-HUMAN because creative mode is not discoverable in `dsh-superagent`, `dsh-superagent-prototype`, `dsh-next-steps`, the installed DSH packages or the live profiles; no install was attempted and no restart was substituted. #58 is additionally BLOCKED because #46 failed review. Each carries backup, creative-mode, load/composer-empty-dock/harness_status verification, rollback and original-issue reporting. Recorded overlap: Phase 0's `dsh-next-steps` contract sits on the dock rewrite, so the slim restore must prove both behaviors survive or roll back.

Questions answered: Phase 0's screenshot question is resolved by the #54 decision (accept unit/component + report); the default-model drift is resolved by PR #49 matching the live Gemini/OpenRouter decision. Two true decisions remain: (1) how is creative mode invoked (blocks #55–#57; if it does not exist, which apply path replaces it); (2) remove the inline secret fallbacks found in #50 now, or keep them with rotation deferred.

No PR was merged, approved, closed, edited, pushed to or auto-merged; no service restarted; no secret or key touched; no live working tree modified. Limitation: branches for #39/#40/#44 exist only in local worktrees; #46 needs a fix on `dsh-superagent-prototype#4` and re-review.

Follow-up for trigger `6c91cbda7e262a7a62f112b1869ef04a` is fully complete and **ready**: all 3 pull requests ([PR #70](https://github.com/gera3d/superagent-sandbox/pull/70), [PR #72](https://github.com/gera3d/superagent-sandbox/pull/72), [PR #74](https://github.com/gera3d/superagent-sandbox/pull/74)) received formal **PASS** review verdicts on GitHub, and the run summary is posted to [issue #54 comment 6639815524](https://github.com/gera3d/superagent-sandbox/issues/54#issuecomment-6639815524).
